svg.title: Perfect octave (P8): information sheet
svg.desc: Perfect octave, P8: C4 to C5, 12 semitones. A keyboard from C4 to C5 with both keys highlighted in this interval's identity colour and 12 numbered semitone hops. Two time strips show the notes one after another and together. Plogger is not applicable at the boundary.

g.text: 8 letter names counted inclusively (C to C)
HOW TO READ THE THREE PLOGGER MARKS
perfect-group family. A family label, not a
A historic teaching lens from the archived
acoustic law. The identity colour is a separate,
Next lower: Major seventh (M7, 11 semitones). Root C4 stays; upper note C5→B4, one key apart.
How to read: find C4 on your keyboard, then count 12 semitones up (every key, white or
black, is one step) to C5. The numbered arcs are those steps. Top left shows the two notes
one after another, top right the same two notes together.
